newsitem.title: UK: MSAS details first half 1997 performance.
newsitem.headline: MSAS details first half 1997 performance.

text.p: UK global freight forwarder, MSAS Cargo International Ltd said that in first half 1997 Asia-Pacific once again produced an excellent overall result, with Malaysia and Singapore performing particularly strongly.
Margins in Hong Kong came under some pressure early in the year, but is "confident of a good outcome for Hong Kong and China in the second half, " it said in a statement.

Japan's first half suffered in comparison with 1996 with reduced volumes from a number of major customers but Korea's performance improved as MSAS's new organisation consolidated its market position, it added.

In Australia's profitability continued to be affected by price reductions in the customs clearance market, and New Zealand acquired a major new customer for the second half of the year, the New Zealand Department of Defence, the statement said.
Also contributing to growth was the establishment of a new logistics centre in Kuala Lumpur, where Minolta is the principal customer, and a new facility in Dublin, it added.
Other important factors were the continued growth of MSAS Logistics Services in Belgium, and the impact of a full six months management of the Gillette European warehousing activity near Frankfurt.
The company's U.S. organisation produced "excellent profit growth with margin and productivity improvements" continuing to boost performance, but Canada was again disappointing, MSAS said.
Europe produced good operating profit growth, driven by excellent results in Germany, the UK, the Netherlands, and its Finnish operation set up a year ago.
However Spain and France did not perform well in the first half, but increased focus on customer development gives grounds for some optimism in the rest of the year, the statement said.
